instruction:
Start from each `Patient` record; combine it with each `Laboratory` record for which identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`) equals identification of the patient (`Laboratory.ID`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which AST liver enzyme level (`Laboratory.GOT`) is at least 60; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) A ÷ B. Here A is the number of records in the group whose the value of the first rule that applies: if primary diagnosed disease (`Patient.Diagnosis`) matches the pattern '%SLE%' (ASCII letters match regardless of case; % stands for any run of characters and _ for one) then identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`); otherwise 0 is not missing; B is the number of records in the group whose identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`) is not missing.
Conventions (SQLite's semantics): a condition that involves a missing value is undetermined, and neither it nor its negation holds. A formula is missing when any value in it is missing. Numbers are 64-bit integers or IEEE double-precision reals: ÷ is real-valued division (floating point); a division by 0 is missing; +, − and × of whole numbers stay whole unless the result leaves the 64-bit range, when it becomes a real; a sum of whole numbers that leaves that range is an error. a mod b is the remainder after both are truncated to whole numbers (missing when b truncates to 0). round rounds the double-precision value, halves away from zero; trunc truncates toward zero; text of a whole number is its decimal digits; sqrt, log10 and ln of a value outside their domain are missing; first_present is the first of its values that is not missing; nullif(a, b) is a, or missing when a equals b; larger and smaller are missing when any of their values is missing. Text is compared character by character, upper and lower case distinct (except in pattern matching). A date part of a value that is not a date is missing. When grouping or removing duplicates, missing values count as equal to each other.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.Diagnosis LIKE '%SLE%' THEN T1.ID ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.`GOT` >= 60

Start from each `Patient` record; combine it with each `Laboratory` record for which identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`) equals identification of the patient (`Laboratory.ID`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); combine it with each `Examination` record for which identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`) equals identification of the patient (`Examination.ID`), one combined record per match (a record without a match is dropped); keep only the records for which all of the following hold: [1] prothrombin time (`Laboratory.PT`) is less than 14; [2] thrombosis severity grade (`Examination.Thrombosis`) is less than 3; [3] thrombosis severity grade (`Examination.Thrombosis`) is greater than 0 [end]; all kept records form one group, which gives one result row; for each result row, return (1) the number of records in the group whose identification of the patient (`Patient.ID`) is not missing.
Conventions (SQLite's semantics): a condition that involves a missing value is undetermined, and neither it nor its negation holds. A formula is missing when any value in it is missing. Numbers are 64-bit integers or IEEE double-precision reals: ÷ is real-valued division (floating point); a division by 0 is missing; +, − and × of whole numbers stay whole unless the result leaves the 64-bit range, when it becomes a real; a sum of whole numbers that leaves that range is an error. a mod b is the remainder after both are truncated to whole numbers (missing when b truncates to 0). round rounds the double-precision value, halves away from zero; trunc truncates toward zero; text of a whole number is its decimal digits; sqrt, log10 and ln of a value outside their domain are missing; first_present is the first of its values that is not missing; nullif(a, b) is a, or missing when a equals b; larger and smaller are missing when any of their values is missing. Text is compared character by character, upper and lower case distinct (except in pattern matching). A date part of a value that is not a date is missing. When grouping or removing duplicates, missing values count as equal to each other.
reference_sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID INNER JOIN Examination AS T3 ON T1.ID = T3.ID WHERE T2.PT < 14 AND T3.Thrombosis < 3 AND T3.Thrombosis > 0
